newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures seen opening lower, trade sideways.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures seen opening lower, trade sideways.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures were called to open lower Thursday and then trade sideways through the day with little news and very limited heating demand, industry sources said.
November Henry Hub futures were expected to open at $2.079 per million British thermal units, down less than two cents from Wednesday's close at $2.096, the brokers and marketers said.
November was also pegged near $2.079 in over the counter discussion early Thursday, the sources said.
November traded down 2.4 cents at $2.072 per mmBtu in ACCESS trade after hitting a low of $2.045, and ended with offers at $2.079
November prices were in part pushed lower in ACCESS trade by bearish AGA storage data Wednesday, the sources said.
Technically, traders assessed November support in the $2.00 area, with resistance at $2.12 and then at the recent high of $2.305.
If November were to break the $2.04 mark however, it would likely trade down to $2.015, with further support then pegged at $1.98 per mmBtu, the sources said.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
